title: The Floating Gimmick
text: “So after monsters, we’ve got accessories that boost the abilities of humans, demi-humans, and beastmen too, huh?”
“Seems it can be used for Class Ups too. Apparently it works as a catalyst that boosts the abilities of anyone with the matching attribute.”
“Amazing… For demi-humans and beastmen, it says it ‘awakens ancient blood.’”
“What a treasure trove, honestly.”
“I wonder what would happen if we had Sadeena-san hold one, or used it for a Class Up?”

Later, when we had someone from the kingdom check it out, apparently it was confirmed that for beastmen with high water-attribute aptitude, it drastically lowered the level required to unlock a further transformation, I say. In Siltvelt, it seems the Aotatsu tribe—like that pig who was with Takt—became able to transform into a dragon form.
“Sounds like Sadeena-san could end up in her true orca form with something like that.”
“Yeah.”
“Seems like she could already do that even now, though.”
“In Wild Naofumi’s world, apparently there was a remnant ability to transform, left over from when her body was modified into something like a walrus, nano.”
Ah, that’s a mighty lively version of Father, I say. Brings back memories, indeed.
“I mean… what exactly does that Naofumi think Sadeena-san is, seriously?”
“That was a Naofumi eaten away by all sorts of nasty curses, so you shouldn’t think too hard about it, nano.”

“So this time we got something for water-attribute aptitude, but I bet there are other accessories out there too—ones that could draw out abilities like Lars-chan’s or Fohl-kun’s transformation skills.”
“Larsazusa-san is bamboo… well, a plant, so that’d be earth, I suppose. And Fohl-san’s aptitude was the beast attribute, wasn’t it?”
“Honestly, my only thought is ‘this dungeon took way too long to get to.’”
“Isn’t that fine, though? Someone in a future era better than us can just make good use of it.”
“Though it’ll probably get abused too.”

After chatting like that, Father went back to exploring in earnest, I say. Past the boss, we found a weapon closely resembling the harpoon Older Sister had once salvaged, I say. Ah, nostalgic. That was the precursor skill to Brionac, indeed. Never used anymore these days. Once we picked up the weapon and moved on… we came out into an area that, despite being underwater, had fish and nut symbols painted on it. The fish symbols only continued partway, and beyond that it was nuts only, it seemed. On our screen, it just kept going up and up, out of view.
“Uhh…”
Father had been peering way up past the boundary line, but then he turned his face toward the screen.
“Naofumi-san. Please don’t look this way.”
Reading the mood, Itsuki stepped out of the circle and spoke up.
“Itsuki, you’re up. Don’t try to pin this on Naofumi and run.”

“No, no, we should just backtrack and explore somewhere else! There’s probably a mechanism to drain the water, and we’re meant to come here after that. Or maybe this is a scrapped map that got flooded due to some accident or defect!”

Itsuki tried to reason out the dungeon’s structure. But given everything we’d seen so far, it seemed highly unlikely this dungeon had that kind of flaw, I say. Besides, water or not, the layout was clearly built so only Father could swim through it.
“It’s true this dungeon was sealed away for a long time, so there is a possibility, nano.”
“Exactly! So let’s head back for now!”
Rival took Itsuki’s side here, I say. This was where I had to voice my objection.
“No, I’m certain this is a gimmick where Itsuki does a character change and just bobs on up, I say.”
I, too, was a modern man who’d dabbled in video games, indeed. Looking at all the gimmicks so far, the optimal solution was easy enough to imagine.
“Yeah. Probably there are spikes or something ahead, and Itsuki’s got to float up while dodging left and right. The map layout suggests something’s there too.”
Ren grabbed Itsuki’s arm as he tried to flee, so I grabbed his other arm to match, and together we hauled Itsuki over to the bow circle, I say.
“Ren-san! Motoyasu-san! Let go of me! This isn’t my turn!”

“No, no, this is definitely a doable gimmick. From the looks of it, this dungeon works like the last one—if you hit a spike or take a fatal hit, you just get kicked out of the dungeon. So go get smashed up already.”
“Why do these gimmicks have to be so elaborate?! I’ll curse whoever designed this labyrinth!”
Itsuki thrashed about in resistance! Now, now, settle down, I say.
“I—I can’t become a spectacle in a place like this! Rafuemon-san! Rishia-san! Help me!”
“Fweeeeeeeeeh!?”
“Itsuki-kun!”
Itsuki, ever the sore loser, cried out for rescue, I say.
“Give it up, Itsuki, the goal might be right past this. We can’t let this slide.”
“Enough talk, just go, I say! Father, here comes Itsuki—go!”
With a solid kick, I sent Itsuki into the circle and demanded Father perform the character change, I say.
“Naofumi! Go!”
“Man… wish I could’ve been the one to go. Good luck, Itsuki.”
“Waaaaaaah!”

With a whoosh, Father activated a skill that generated a bubble barrier of oxygen around himself, and after pressing his hands together as if praying for good fortune, he performed the character change with Itsuki. Instantly, Itsuki began breathing the air from the bubble barrier Father had left behind, cheeks puffed out like a Riska, and started climbing up through the Riska-exclusive zone.
“Glob glob glob! Blub blub blub!”

Itsuki, apparently taking his frustration out on us, fired off a barrage of bullets straight at the screen. Hard to see, indeed. Flashbangs mixed in too, it seemed—flash after flash going off—but Itsuki kept steadily floating his way up through the water.
“I see, nano, so that’s how it works, nano.”
“…I do feel sorry for Bow Hero-sama.”
“I mean, personally I think it’d be nicer if the floating gimmick at least wrapped you in a bubble or something.”
“Hmm… floating on up he goes.”
Rival, Fiancée, Father, and Sakura-chan all followed Itsuki’s ascent with their eyes, I say.
“Fweeh… Itsuki-sama… just a little more, hang in there…”
“Right, left… ah, this is so frustrating… I can’t move at all underwater.”
“Wait, can’t Rafuemon swim? I’d have figured Rafumi-chan and the others modified him to be waterproof by now.”
“Huh? I wonder. I’ll ask Rafumi and the others about it later.”

While chatting about such things, we watched the scene of Itsuki breaking through the gimmick, I say. Incidentally, as for what happened afterward—Itsuki got his revenge by shoving Ren into the sea. And so, with a great splash, Itsuki finally broke through the Riska-exclusive underwater floating zone and emerged from the surface.
“Pahh! Finally made it to the surface!”
Itsuki hauled himself up onto the nearest patch of land with a splash and caught his breath, indeed. The area was now one where a character change was possible.
“There’s clearly more ahead, but you’ve made me go this far. I’m going to make absolutely sure I see what kind of prize is waiting!”

Half out of spite, Itsuki stormed into the room ahead that looked like it held some kind of reward. There was some sort of picture drawn on the wall, but light shot out and it opened without us needing to do anything in particular. There seemed to be other places to go from here too, but confirmation came first. Whatever we obtained here was probably going to open up new paths forward. Inside was a stone tablet inscribed with Hero Script, with something written on it. The screen zoomed in, practically demanding our attention.
“Looks like we can learn a spell here. I wonder what kind of spell it’ll be!”
Stomping over with rough, irritated steps, Itsuki examined the Hero Script. It displayed in characters we could all read too—meaning, presumably, it was a spell everyone could learn.
『Let the Bow Hero, source of power, so command. Unravel the workings of all creation once more, and alter the form of that person.』
“Four Fairy Morph… wait, what?!”

With a poof, the effect of the spell Itsuki had just cast reverted him back to his original form! Of course, he was stark naked. Since it was from behind, the screen was fine, indeed. So, this was the kind of incantation it was. At a glance, this incantation might trick you into thinking you could just trace the letters or speak it aloud in Japanese to cast it, but really, it was the magical language—you had to weave your mana and draw out the distinctive characters properly, indeed. But the characters etched here were the genuine article, capable of properly manifesting the spell’s effect. This wasn’t some rigged spell that had merely caused that form to happen before—it meant it could be fully learned and mastered, I say.
